intro.description: This reference cheat sheet guides you through the maintained Eclipse JDT cleanup that replaces eligible Iterator-driven while loops with concise enhanced for loops. Sandbox no longer registers a second cleanup implementation.

item.title: Understand the Transformation
Configure the Standard JDT Cleanup
item.description:
Open the normal Java cleanup dialog:
1. Select Java source in the Package Explorer
2. Choose Source → Clean Up…
3. Select or configure a standard Eclipse JDT cleanup profile
4. Enable the JDT option for conversion to enhanced for loops
5. Review the preview before applying the change
There is no Sandbox Tools cleanup tab or separate Sandbox option.

item.title: Review the Result
item.description:
Verify that:
• the element type is correct
• imports and comments remain appropriate
• the loop body is unchanged
• iterator-specific behavior was not required
Compile and run the relevant tests after accepting the cleanup.

item.title: Know Which Project Owns the Cleanup
item.description: The active cleanup is supplied and maintained by org.eclipse.jdt.ui. The Sandbox feature retains historical source, tests, this cheat sheet, and offline Help only. Active cleanup defects should therefore be reported to Eclipse JDT UI.
